subject: Prohibition era
title: What If a Country Banned Alcohol? America Tried It for 13 Years

scenes.text: What if a country banned alcohol overnight? America did in 1920. It ended with the government poisoning drinks.
At first it worked. Drinking fell by half in five years, and deaths from liver disease dropped.
Then bootleggers started stealing industrial alcohol, meant for paint and fuel, and cleaning it up to sell.
By 1927 the government fought back: factories had to add more poison, including up to 10 percent methanol.
On Christmas Eve 1926, over 60 New Yorkers fell critically ill from one batch. Eight died that day. By some estimates, 10,000 died in all.
scenes.keywords: old hospital ward black and white

scenes.text: In 1933 America gave up. It's the only constitutional amendment the country has ever repealed.

description:
What if a country banned alcohol? The United States did from 1920 to 1933.
Consumption fell by about 30 percent over the period and cirrhosis deaths dropped, but bootleggers turned to industrial alcohol, the government ordered it poisoned with methanol and other chemicals, and by some estimates 10,000 people died from it. The 21st Amendment repealed the ban in 1933, the only repeal of an amendment in US history.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: New York's chief medical examiner said at the time that the government knew poisoning alcohol would not stop people drinking. Which ban should we run through next?
